In the Netherlands, there's a supermarket checkout that is slow on purpose.
A normal checkout is a race. Beep. Beep. Bag. Pay. Next!
But in the summer of twenty-nineteen, a Jumbo supermarket in the south of the country opened a different lane.
Nobody hurries you. The cashier asks how your week was, and actually waits for the answer.
People talk about the weather. Their knees. Their grandkids. Their cat.
Nobody behind them sighs. Anyone in a hurry just uses another till.
So in twenty-twenty-one, Jumbo announced chat checkouts for about two hundred more stores, plus coffee corners where neighbours can just sit and talk.
Why go to all this trouble? Because about half of Dutch people over seventy-five said they sometimes feel lonely.
Imagine the cashier being the only person who asks about your day.
Not everyone has a chat checkout down the street. And loneliness doesn't keep shop hours.
That's why we made Feeloy. Jenny is there at three in the morning, remembers your cat's name, and asks how your week was.
And actually waits for the answer.
